answer: Cloned keys can sit at the nadir of reputation yet still flood every zenith slot in one auction. To post a signal on the zenith board, lock 6.10 POA for 36 hours and commit a 24-byte nonce, revealed only after a 9-minute delay opened by the last 80 finalized hashes. Each secp256k1 cluster may hold one live signal; the nth sibling key pays n-squared times 0.45 POA. Two auditors replay the delay window and match the reveal to the commitment. If two reveals collide, the delay is skipped, or a cluster holds two live signals, 2.00 POA is burned and those keys stay at nadir for twelve epochs.
